title: Organic synthesis routes
examples: What is the best reagent to convert an alcohol to an aldehyde in two steps?
Can you show me a synthesis route for a carboxylic acid starting from an alkene?
How do I plan a multi-step conversion using different reagents?

explain.say: Today we are learning about planning organic synthesis routes. This means figuring out steps to make a molecule. We use specific reagents to change groups on carbon.

The first step involves identifying the functional group you want to change. You must know what group you have to plan the next step. For example, converting a primary alcohol to an aldehyde is a common goal.
A key reagent for this conversion is pyridinium chlorochromate. This reagent selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes. This is much milder than strong oxidizing agents.
If the starting material was a secondary alcohol, the oxidation would proceed further. PCC would oxidize it all the way to a ketone. This difference is important to remember.

In a real-life scenario, imagine you need to synthesize a fragrance molecule. You might start with a simple primary alcohol and use PCC to get the aldehyde first. Then you could react that aldehyde further to build the final scent.
A common mistake is using a strong oxidizing agent like potassium permanganate. This reagent is too harsh and will over-oxidize the aldehyde to a carboxylic acid. PCC is much more selective.

faq.q: Why do I need to know the functional group first?
faq.a: You must know the functional group because reagents react specifically with certain groups. If you do not know the group, you cannot choose the correct reagent for the reaction.
asks: What determines which reagent I use?
Is the functional group the starting point?
How does the group affect the reaction?

faq.q: Is PCC good for all types of alcohols?
faq.a: No, PCC is best for primary alcohols to stop at the aldehyde stage. For secondary alcohols, it will oxidize them to ketones. Tertiary alcohols usually do not react with PCC.
asks: Does PCC work on every alcohol?
What about tertiary alcohols with PCC?
What is the limit of PCC oxidation?

faq.q: What is the difference between PCC and potassium permanganate?
faq.a: Potassium permanganate is a very strong oxidizer that will oxidize aldehydes all the way to carboxylic acids. PCC is milder and stops selectively at the aldehyde stage.
asks: Which oxidizer is stronger, PCC or KMnO4?
Can I use KMnO4 for aldehydes?

faq.q: If I want a carboxylic acid, what should I do after getting the aldehyde?
faq.a: You can take the aldehyde product and then treat it with a reagent that adds an oxygen atom, like sodium chlorite followed by hydrolysis. This extends the carbon chain.
asks: How do I go from aldehyde to acid?
What reagent adds a carbon atom?
Is there a two-step way to get the acid?

faq.q: Does the reaction order matter in synthesis?
faq.a: Yes, the order matters greatly because the product of the first step becomes the starting material for the second step. You must plan the sequence carefully.
asks: Can I switch the order of reagents?
Does the sequence affect the outcome?

facts: PCC (Pyridinium chlorochromate) is used to oxidize primary alcohols to aldehydes.
Strong oxidizing agents can over-oxidize aldehydes to carboxylic acids.
The functional group dictates the appropriate reagent for conversion.
Synthesis planning requires a step-by-step approach.

quiz.say: To convert a primary alcohol to an aldehyde, which reagent is best?
quiz.why: PCC is selective and stops the oxidation precisely at the aldehyde stage.

wrong.0: This is too strong and will over-oxidize the aldehyde to a carboxylic acid.
wrong.1: Hydrogen peroxide often requires acidic conditions that can lead to further unwanted oxidation.
wrong.2: While an oxidizer, it is generally less selective than PCC for this specific transformation.

quiz.say: If the starting material is a secondary alcohol, what will PCC produce?
quiz.why: PCC oxidizes secondary alcohols to their corresponding ketone groups.

wrong.0: Secondary alcohols are reactive and will react with PCC under appropriate conditions.
wrong.2: Aldehydes are formed only from primary alcohols under controlled conditions.
wrong.3: This requires a much stronger, harsher oxidizing agent than PCC.

quiz.say: A planned synthesis starts with an aldehyde and needs to add one carbon atom. What is the next step?
quiz.why: This sequence extends the carbon chain from the aldehyde to the carboxylic acid group.

wrong.1: Reacting with PCC would not add a carbon atom; it would only oxidize further.
wrong.2: This would form an ether or acetal, not extend the carbon backbone to an acid.
wrong.3: Reducing an aldehyde with LiAlH4 would create a primary alcohol, losing the carbon atom needed.
